concepts.def: The migration of the Prophet Muhammad and the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah, the event from which the Islamic calendar is dated.
The community of Muslims founded at Madinah, bound together by faith rather than tribe or family.
An agreement organising relations between the Muslims and the Jewish and other tribes of Madinah, including mutual defence of the city.
The emigrants from Makkah (Muhajirun) and the helpers of Madinah (Ansar), paired in brotherhood so homes and wealth were shared.
The battles of Badr in 624, Uhud in 625 and the Trench in 627 tested and ultimately secured the survival of the young community.
After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in 628, the Muslims took Makkah largely peacefully in 630, and the Ka'bah was cleared of idols.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Islam: The First Islamic Community — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Islam: The First Islamic Community brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Islam: The First Islamic Community.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the Hijrah refer to?
options: The migration of the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE
The first revelation of the Qur'an
The pilgrimage to Makkah
The Prophet's night journey to Jerusalem
The Muslims of Madinah who helped the emigrants from Makkah
The leaders of the Quraysh in Makkah
The emigrants who left Makkah
The scribes who wrote down the Qur'an

mcqs.q: Which battle of 624 was the first major Muslim victory?
options: Badr
Uhud
The Trench
Hunayn

mcqs.q: What happened when the Muslims entered Makkah in 630?
options: The city was taken largely peacefully, the idols were removed from the Ka'bah, and a general amnesty was given
The city was burned to the ground
The Muslims were driven out again
The Ka'bah was demolished

mcqs.q: Was the Hijrah simply an escape from danger?
options: Membership of the ummah depended on wealth.
The Hijrah was just a retreat with no lasting significance.
The Hijrah was a pilgrimage made every year by the early Muslims.

No - it was the founding moment of the Islamic community: in Madinah the Muslims built their own institutions, and the Islamic calendar dates from the Hijrah, not from the Prophet's birth or first revelation.

mcqs.q: Was the new community in Madinah organised around tribal loyalty?
options: Membership of the ummah depended on wealth.
The Hijrah was a pilgrimage made every year by the early Muslims.
Early Islam kept the old tribal system unchanged.
No - the ummah replaced tribal loyalty with loyalty based on faith, with the Muhajirun and Ansar paired as brothers across old tribal lines.

mcqs.q: Did only Muslims live in early Madinah?
options: Madinah under the Prophet was a city with no non-Muslim inhabitants.
Madinah was an empty desert before the Muslims arrived.
The Hijrah was a pilgrimage made every year by the early Muslims.
No - the Charter of Madinah included the Jewish and other tribes of the city, setting out mutual rights and duties, including joint defence.

sequence.def: 610 AD: the Qur'an begins on Mount Hira
c.613 AD: open call to Islam starts
c.615 AD: persecuted Muslims seek refuge
622 AD: the ummah established in Madinah
624 AD: small Muslim force defeats Makkah
630 AD: the city submits; idols destroyed
